name: CDW (enterprise IT distributor) - accelerator and GPU-server supply
notes: QUOTE-ONLY for the high-value SKUs; price_usd deliberately null. Process verified on the product pages themselves: 'Get a Quote' / 'Request Pricing' forms requiring name, email, phone and organization, with the stated SLA 'A CDW representative will email you within one business day to confirm your request'. THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING IN THIS RECORD IS A NEGATIVE ONE: a CDW catalog search for 'NVIDIA H100' returns 676 hits, but the entire 'Servers & Server Management' facet is only 8 items and the accelerator content is L40S, L4, RTX PRO/6000 Ada, RTX 5000 Ada, RTX A1000/A400, BlueField-3 and ConnectX - i.e. CDW stocks workstation and inference-class PCIe cards and the DGX, and does NOT list H100/A100/H200 SXM modules at all. The 353 items in the '$3000 and above' bucket are almost entirely servers and complete systems, not accelerator modules. So 'CDW carries H100' is false at the module level; the real question is whether a DGX or HGX system can be quoted, and DGX B200 8x180GB is listed (CDW # 8055598, mfg DGXB-G1440+P2CMI36, includes full 3-year support) at quote-only. OBSERVED LEAD TIMES from the product pages (2026-10-03): RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96GB '4-6+ Weeks'; ConnectX-7 '1-3+ Days'; RTX 6000 Ada 48GB shown as 'discontinued on October 3, 2026' - a live example of a datacentre GPU SKU ageing out of a distributor catalogue inside a product generation. CDW's own price filter note ('Does not show contract pricing or discounts') plus the absence of any price on the accelerator pages is why nothing is recorded numerically. EXPORT CONTROLLED (true). Regime: US BIS advanced-computing export controls (the Oct 2023 interim final rule, 88 FR 73458 - source sup-buy-bis-2023-advanced-computing-controls), which put datacenter accelerators under ECCN 3A090/4A090, added the advanced-computing Foreign Direct Product (FDP) rule, and extended Regional Stability (RS) controls to Country Groups D:1, D:4 and D:5. For items destined to Macau or Country Group D:5 the rule applies a PRESUMPTION OF DENIAL; other RS destinations get a presumption of approval. Practical effect: which accelerator you can legally be sold, and which SKU counts as compliant, is set by destination and end user - not by the channel.
